business.description: Sarla Performance Fibers Limited specialises in the production and export of polyester and nylon textured, twisted, and dyed yarns, including covered yarns, high-tenacity yarns, and sewing threads. The company has evolved from a manufacturer of basic yarns into a strategically focused producer of complex, high-value yarns with deep customisation capabilities.

outlook.statement: Targeting revenue growth of approximately 15% in FY 2026-27, supported by expected recovery in demand across key export markets, continued expansion of value-added product portfolio, and ongoing operational efficiency initiatives. Long-term objective of sustaining EBITDA margins above 20% remains firmly intact.

Medium to long-term outlook for the Indian MMF and textile industry remains highly encouraging, supported by favourable trade developments, strengthening global competitiveness, proposed FTAs with UK and EU, and gradual normalisation of geopolitical conditions. India-US trade agreement discussions provide additional optimism.

The outlook for the global textile market in FY 2026-27 is cautiously constructive, shaped by the developments and structural shifts of FY 2025-26. The partial tariff rationalisation achieved through bilateral framework agreements provides a degree of stability. The China Plus One strategy is expected to deepen further. Retail sentiment is expected to improve gradually as inflation moderates and consumer spending stabilises, supporting a recovery in order flows across apparel and home textiles. Demand for man-made fibres, technical textiles, and sustainable fabrics is projected to grow at a healthy pace.

India's economic outlook for FY 2026-27 remains cautiously optimistic, with the RBI projecting GDP growth of approximately 6.6% and several institutions forecasting a range of 6.5% to 7.0%. Private consumption is expected to be supported by income tax relief, GST rate rationalisation, above-normal monsoon, and sustained real income gains from declining inflation.

Domestic revenue share projected to grow from 39% in FY26 to 55-60% over next few years; nylon sales volume projected to reach ~60% from 49% in FY26; value-added products portfolio on track for full-scale benefits by FY27; targeting 10% share of overall Indian market with 4-5% improvement in operating margins from domestic contribution.

India textile sector: domestic consumption strong growth driver; export growth aided by India-UK and India-EU FTAs; MMF, technical textiles, sustainable apparel present strong medium-term opportunities; companies investing in capacity, technology, ESG, product innovation well-placed to capture disproportionate growth share.

Global MMF market valued at ~USD 175 billion in 2024, projected to grow to USD 258 billion by 2028 at 7.9% CAGR; polyester fibre market valued at ~USD 130 billion in 2024, expected to reach USD 207 billion by 2034 at 4.5% CAGR; global yarn/fiber/thread market valued at ~USD 122 billion in 2025, projected to reach USD 160 billion by 2030 at 5.4% CAGR.

The Company's robust customer relationships and a favourable policy environment — including supportive tariff structures that enhanced India's competitiveness as a sourcing hub — provided a strong foundation for sustained growth. Global sourcing dynamics continued to evolve in response to tariff escalations and geopolitical realignments, positioning India as a preferred destination due to its stable policy framework and integrated manufacturing capabilities.
To continually improve customer satisfaction worldwide and pioneer the development of new speciality products.

The Company continues to pursue its established business strategy of expanding its presence in international markets, optimising its product mix, and strengthening long-term customer relationships across European, American, and Asian markets. No extraordinary measures are considered necessary given that the inadequacy of profits arose solely from a one-time exceptional item and not from any adverse change in the Company's business operations or outlook.
